title: Seaglass tactical implementation checklist
content:
Seaglass field sprint scratchpad - quick notes and action items

Context:
- Onboarding Seaglass for Private (VPC) deployment. They require HSM-backed key management, strict egress rules, and ability to pin model variant per route. Customer is in EU, wants predictable latency ~<120ms p50 for 4k context.

Today (2026-02-20) objectives:
- Finalize KMS/HSM integration checklist with Security (Tomás)
- Validate private control plane connectivity across their VPN + Azure ExpressRoute
- Proof-run canary of model-1 -> fallback to model-1-quant when capacity low

Top priorities (checklist):
[ ] Confirm HSM vendor (Thales) onboarding steps documented and contact scheduled
[ ] Add ingress egress allowlist in customer's firewall config (need IP ranges from infra)
[ ] Apply helm chart overrides for resource requests / limits (gpu: a10g, mem: 64Gi)
[ ] Create rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback after 3 failed inferences
[ ] Run load test (k6) at 100rps for 30m, capture token-level cost delta

Config snippets & commands (copy as-needed):
- Helm values (override):
  redwood:
    model:
      name: seaglass-llm-13b
      pin: v2026-02-17
    runtime:
      gpuType: a10g
      replicas: 2
- kubectl apply -f ingress-allowlist.yaml --context=seaglass-prod
- curl -X POST https://private.redwood.example/api/v1/rollouts -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{\"policy\":\"canary\",\"steps\": [5,25,100]}'

Quick troubleshooting notes:
- If KV cache misses spike after model swap, check envoy route header passthrough (need x-rw-kv-key TTL mapping)
- Symptoms of HSM auth failing: 401 with 'kms:unauthorized', check signed cert chain on customer side and OCI region mapping

Open questions / blockers:
- Do they require audit logs to be forwarded to their Splunk instance or Redwood-hosted retention is ok? (Leah to confirm)
- Exact latency SLO for burst traffic (>200 concurrent sessions) - product asked for hard numbers
- Are GPUs ephemeral on their private infra? If yes, we must add persistent cache layer (redis) for KV cache warmup

Notes to self:
- Keep play-by-play in this file during pairing calls to avoid scatter. Paste relevant ticket numbers inline.
- When in doubt about model quantization impact on hallucination rates, run our prompt-eval harness against the customer's 50-sample prompt set.

Next steps / owners:
- Tomás: HSM onboarding checklist + scheduled call with Thales (due 2026-02-22)
- Leah: Confirm Splunk/retention requirements (due 2026-02-21)
- Devon: Prepare k6 script & baseline token-cost report (due 2026-02-23)
- Ishani (me): Coordinate canary rollout and monitor logs during first 2 hours after deploy

Random TODOs / reminders:
- Save kubeconfig snapshot to secure folder (encrypt before upload)
- Request temporary access for Seaglass SRE to read-only console for 48h
- Add a short 'what to expect' README for their infra team explaining our fallback behavior

End of scratchpad - will clean up and move final checklist into Confluence when stable.
